students.ThoughtsLowInvestment:
Hina
She has naturally over-the-top numbers on her skills that means she just needs levels and gear to deal with campaign. Her AOE is wide and long and reliable enough to clear waves alone if properly aimed.

Her EX has high cost but I believe it is worth the cost especially when you have some trouble clearing stages -- 7-Cost-EX that kills everyone is worth more than two 4-cost-EXes to kill one area after all (or two 4-cost-EXes to damage, but not kill, everyone). Her multipliers also mean that she can be used in Yellow stages (Maybe even blue but not sure if blue can be dealt with a minimal Hina, probably can but I have no first-hand experience on this)

This is the reason why Early JP BA had her on top of the reroll tier lists.

And if you don't think her EX is worth using, shes still the best red AA in the game if you happen to have an AA slot in your team. 

Something to note however is that the moment you stop NEEDING her overkill EX power, her EX will have far less value because suddenly you can just kill with 4 cost - This is the reason why "7 cost too expensive" or "Needs Ui lmao (she never did need Ui)" happened after everyone got enough invesstments to kill waves without needing 7 cost. This is true for all stages of progression.
students.ThoughtsLateGame:
Hina
Hina's evaluation for raids is essentially the same as in PVE/Progression. Except we now look at it at high investments. She still has over the top numbers that will definitely be of use to any Red or Yellow raid whether using her EX or using her AA or both. 

The issue she faces is also similar, and that is the easier it is to finish the raid, the less impactful she is. Hina is someone that will see the most value during the periods where a raid is still actually HARD and not a cakewalk. This does mean that she will always shine whenever there is a new difficulty tho wink wink.

students.ThoughtsLowInvestment:
Hina
She has naturally over-the-top numbers on her skills that means she just needs levels and gear to deal with campaign. Her AOE is wide and long and reliable enough to clear waves alone if properly aimed.

Her EX has high cost but I believe it is worth the cost especially when you have some trouble clearing stages -- 7-Cost-EX that kills everyone is worth more than two 4-cost-EXes to kill one area after all (or two 4-cost-EXes to damage, but not kill, everyone). Her multipliers also mean that she can be used in Yellow stages (Maybe even blue but not sure if blue can be dealt with a minimal Hina, probably can but I have no first-hand experience on this)

This is the reason why Early JP BA had her on top of the reroll tier lists.

And if you don't think her EX is worth using, shes still the best red AA in the game if you happen to have an AA slot in your team. 

Something to note however is that the moment you stop NEEDING her overkill EX power, her EX will have far less value because suddenly you can just kill with 4 cost - This is the reason why "7 cost too expensive" or "Needs Ui lmao (she never did need Ui)" happened after everyone got enough invesstments to kill waves without needing 7 cost. This is true for all stages of progression.
students.ThoughtsLateGame:
Hina
Hina's evaluation for raids is essentially the same as in PVE/Progression. Except we now look at it at high investments. She still has over the top numbers that will definitely be of use to any Red or Yellow raid whether using her EX or using her AA or both. 

The issue she faces is also similar, and that is the easier it is to finish the raid, the less impactful she is. Hina is someone that will see the most value during the periods where a raid is still actually HARD and not a cakewalk. This does mean that she will always shine whenever there is a new difficulty tho wink wink.

If you thought Mika was "broken" wait till you hear about Hina (Dress). I generally don't want to do direct student comparisons for these thoughts but I think this is quite an apt comparison due to both of their availability, roles, and impact.

I won't explain her kit, you can look it up yourself. What I will say however is that with the "usual" buffs, against a high HP normal armor target, DHina's AVERAGE EX damage is equal to Mika's AVERAGE EX damage at 100% HP. With no buffs, Mika loses. However with more buffs, Mika does edge out more at 80%+ HP and loses afterwards.

Emphasis on "High HP" and "Normal Armor" because this is where it gets interesting. Firstly, High HP matters because in the comparison with Mika, high HP means each damage has less impact on Mika's extra multiplier so Mika performs as close to peak performance as possible... and she either loses or barely evens out. Next, normal armor: Note that Color Effectiveness buffs are part of both of these two students' kits which means their damage will further get multiplied against the correct color. The difference is that Mika gets 50% and DHina gets... 130%. this means that against their favored colors, DHina will always do more assuming the same target just with different armor.

Moving on to the next stage: "Malding"
What are the only three things that people mald for with Mika? Answer: Survival, Stability, Shitty Accuracy.
Survival: Mika is frontline, so chances are shes gonna get hit a lot unless you have a dedicated tank. But people tend to avoid this option when trying to mald for score. How about DHina? DHina is a backliner. So she won't really get hit outside of AOEs. Next, she's MG which is the tankiest type of backliner and she's Elastic armor so at most she takes x1 damage. This means that if she's dying to AOE you might as well not bring any backliner that isnt resist armor. However, survival issue is really only relevant against Red damaging bosses and otherwise Mika actually can serve as a tank (but in DHina's defense you can just bring SHoshi for this lol).
Stability: Mika has guaranteed crit so people can afford to just reset for better stability, the sad part here is that malding for stability feels so awful since the variance on the possible damage dealt from stability is massive. Unlike crit which is a Crit or Not. Additionally, stability is in the end a minor damage difference so unless you're going for a hyper specific strat (I'm looking at you Chesed 1Core) you generally won't do this. How about DHina? She gets PERFECT stability so you get to ignore the annoying part and just focus on crit malding yay. This is easier than you think because all it takes is to crit 1 or 2 times above average to get enough worth as full stability. Also cope because DHina does have crit passive. AALSO her damage won't decrease over time due to hp %.
Shitty Accuracy: Mika or more like Misska has low accuracy so chances are against targets with evasion (Chesed, Black Ranger) people will keep malding her to hit properly. Guess what? DHina somehow gets +450 accuracy for free for a total of 550! That means? goodbye to (most) accuracy related issues.

And yes, this means DHina is not useless outside of red, she just becomes stronger in red. Against yellow she's as effective as an Iori indoors. purely based on EX damage that is.

With that, comparisons should be done. Now focusing on DHina herself:

As mentioned, DHina gets 130% Red effectiveness alone this means that SHoshi's effective boost on her is roughly at 30% which is still big but is not in the gamechanging stage. This means that you actually aren't locked to using SHoshino when you use DHina. So now for multi-teams we have the option to either double Shoshi or double DHina. Fun fact people opted to go for DHina in JP mainly because... she's that strong, you'd need to own someone who can dish out 70% of DHina's damage for SHoshi to be worth taking a 2nd copy of over DHina... for reference this roughly translates to needing a Red Mika.

DHina also introduces a few interesting mechanics to the game: Cease Moving, Flat Stat Buffs, Taunt Immunity, and Rapid Fire EX (this can funnel SHanako and others of the same type btw).

Now that the praise is done, DHina does have a downside. She requires PLAYER SKILL. She has AOE but is quite thin so youll need to aim properly to take advantage of it. Her successive EX skills are also time senstiive if you're minmaxing but this is irrelevant for most people as you can just take the extra 0.1s delay in firing.

That's about it without delving into the details. This is already long and its gonna get a lot longer if I cover other stuff like them introducing native def pierce and such. But I started with a Mika comparison, I'll end it with another. Just like Mika, in the end she is still just another DPS. However, unlike Mika, DHina doesn't stop at doubling other students' damage, she goes further and even allows for AOE.

She has a Basic skill with Stun that will activate often enough to matter and has just enough value to make a difference in CC required. She obviously can't solo fill the CC gauge but she has enough to prevent you from needing to mald for say, 100% Kayoko and Karin procs.

What I will say however is that with the "usual" buffs, against a high HP normal armor target, DHina's AVERAGE EX damage is equal to Mika's AVERAGE EX damage at 100% HP. With no buffs, Mika loses. However with more buffs, Mika does edge out more at 80%+ HP and loses afterwards.

Emphasis on "High HP" and "Normal Armor" because this is where it gets interesting. Firstly, High HP matters because in the comparison with Mika, high HP means each damage has less impact on Mika's extra multiplier so Mika performs as close to peak performance as possible... and she either loses or barely evens out. Next, normal armor: Note that Color Effectiveness buffs are part of both of these two students' kits which means their damage will further get multiplied against the correct color. The difference is that Mika gets 50% and DHina gets... 130%. this means that against their favored colors, DHina will always do more assuming the same target just with different armor.

Moving on to the next stage: "Malding"
What are the only three things that people mald for with Mika? Answer: Survival, Stability, Shitty Accuracy.
Survival: Mika is frontline, so chances are shes gonna get hit a lot unless you have a dedicated tank. But people tend to avoid this option when trying to mald for score. How about DHina? DHina is a backliner. So she won't really get hit outside of AOEs. Next, she's MG which is the tankiest type of backliner and she's Elastic armor so at most she takes x1 damage. This means that if she's dying to AOE you might as well not bring any backliner that isnt resist armor. However, survival issue is really only relevant against Red damaging bosses and otherwise Mika actually can serve as a tank (but in DHina's defense you can just bring SHoshi for this lol).
Stability: Mika has guaranteed crit so people can afford to just reset for better stability, the sad part here is that malding for stability feels so awful since the variance on the possible damage dealt from stability is massive. Unlike crit which is a Crit or Not. Additionally, stability is in the end a minor damage difference so unless you're going for a hyper specific strat (I'm looking at you Chesed 1Core) you generally won't do this. How about DHina? She gets PERFECT stability so you get to ignore the annoying part and just focus on crit malding yay. This is easier than you think because all it takes is to crit 1 or 2 times above average to get enough worth as full stability. Also cope because DHina does have crit passive. AALSO her damage won't decrease over time due to hp %.
Shitty Accuracy: Mika or more like Misska has low accuracy so chances are against targets with evasion (Chesed, Black Ranger) people will keep malding her to hit properly. Guess what? DHina somehow gets +450 accuracy for free for a total of 550! That means? goodbye to (most) accuracy related issues.

And yes, this means DHina is not useless outside of red, she just becomes stronger in red. Against yellow she's as effective as an Iori indoors. purely based on EX damage that is.

With that, comparisons should be done. Now focusing on DHina herself:

As mentioned, DHina gets 130% Red effectiveness alone this means that SHoshi's effective boost on her is roughly at 30% which is still big but is not in the gamechanging stage. This means that you actually aren't locked to using SHoshino when you use DHina. So now for multi-teams we have the option to either double Shoshi or double DHina. Fun fact people opted to go for DHina in JP mainly because... she's that strong, you'd need to own someone who can dish out 70% of DHina's damage for SHoshi to be worth taking a 2nd copy of over DHina... for reference this roughly translates to needing a Red Mika.

DHina also introduces a few interesting mechanics to the game: Cease Moving, Flat Stat Buffs, Taunt Immunity, and Rapid Fire EX (this can funnel SHanako and others of the same type btw).

Now that the praise is done, DHina does have a downside. She requires PLAYER SKILL. She has AOE but is quite thin so youll need to aim properly to take advantage of it. Her successive EX skills are also time senstiive if you're minmaxing but this is irrelevant for most people as you can just take the extra 0.1s delay in firing.

That's about it without delving into the details. This is already long and its gonna get a lot longer if I cover other stuff like them introducing native def pierce and such. But I started with a Mika comparison, I'll end it with another. Just like Mika, in the end she is still just another DPS. However, unlike Mika, DHina doesn't stop at doubling other students' damage, she goes further and even allows for AOE.

Whenever you summon Iroha's Toramaru, Ibuki will hop in and provide a lot of extra stats to Toramaru. In addition, this turns her EX into a powerful AOE attack that scales off of Toramaru's stats. There are 2 things that are not immediately apparent from this interaction but are actually really useful to know:

1. Ibuki will never take damage while inside Toramaru, even if Toramaru gets damaged by more than its HP could handle. This means she can survive even the most lethal attacks or force enemies to waste a target on Ibuki for things like Peroro Torment's Zap.

2. The mere fact that we can now control Toramaru's Action Queue means we can now manipulate the NS timings to suit our needs. This is especially useful for trying to fit 2 Toramaru NS casts within a short period of time. (e.g. Himari Buff, Peroro Groggy). While this was already possible previously, they were much more sensitive to time and movements prior to this.



Now that's NOT all there is about Ibuki. Without Toramaru, she will still make your team smile with a massive ATK buff so she still serves as a competent striker buffer. She also has the added bonus of actually healing herself so shes less prone to dying. Protecc. She even has an ATK down on her NS so she can also make your team a bit more sustainable.

Note that while in theory you could use her EX to buff Toramaru, it is generally more useful to use that EX card to actually deal damage since otherwise it would just be pushed back to the queue.
